competition: Malaysian National Mathematical Olympiad (OMK), final round, senior (Sulung) category

problems.problem: In triangle $ABC$, let $a,b,c$ be the side lengths opposite $A,B,C$, respectively. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and $AD=t$. Prove that $$t^2=\frac{2b^2+2c^2-a^2}{4}.$$
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{x^2+1}$. Evaluate $$\sum_{k=1}^{2001} f\left(\frac{k}{2001}\right)+\sum_{k=1}^{2000} f\left(\frac{2001}{k}\right).$$

Let $a,b,c$ be the side lengths of triangle $ABC$ opposite the angles $A,B,C$, respectively. Prove that $$\left(\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{b}\right)\cos A+\left(\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}\right)\cos B+\left(\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a}\right)\cos C=3.$$
Let $x,y,z$ be positive real numbers. Prove that $$\frac{x}{y+z}+\frac{y}{x+z}+\frac{z}{x+y}\ge\frac{3}{2}.$$
Determine the greatest positive integer that divides $$n(n+1)^2(n+2)^3(n+3)^4$$ for every integer $n$.
Prove that $5^4+4\cdot 3^{4n}$ is not prime for every positive integer $n$.

Inside a circle with centre $O$ are four congruent circles, with centres $A,B,C,D$ and radius $J$, arranged so that each is tangent to the outer circle and to two of the other circles. A smaller circle, with centre $O$ and radius $j$, is tangent to all four congruent circles. Determine $j$.
Without using a calculator, prove that $$\cos\frac{2\pi}{5}+\cos\frac{4\pi}{5}=-\frac12.$$
Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{2002}$ be positive real numbers such that $$x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_{2002}=2002.$$ Prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^{2002}\frac{x_i}{1+x_i^2}\le\sum_{i=1}^{2002}\frac{1}{1+x_i}.$$
Find all real-valued functions $f$ defined on the positive real numbers such that, for all positive real numbers $x,y$, $$f(xy)=f(x)f(m/y)+f(y)f(m/x),\qquad f(1)=\frac12.$$
Find all real solutions of the system of equations $$x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_{2006}=2006,\qquad x_1^4+x_2^4+\cdots+x_{2006}^4=x_1^3+x_2^3+\cdots+x_{2006}^3.$$
Let $p$ and $q$ be two primes such that $p+q$ and $p-q$ are also primes. Show that $p^2-q$ is also a prime.
Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a^2+b^2+c^2=3$. Prove that $$\frac{1}{1+2ab}+\frac{1}{1+2bc}+\frac{1}{1+2ca}\ge 1.$$

In $\triangle ABC$ the bisectors of the angles $\angle A$, $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ meet the circumcircle at the points $A_1$, $B_1$ and $C_1$ respectively. Let $AA_1\cap CC_1=I$, $AA_1\cap BC=N$ and $BB_1\cap A_1C_1=P$. Denote by $O$ the centre of the circumcircle of $\triangle IPC_1$, and let $OP\cap BC=M$. Find the angles of $\triangle ABC$ if $BM=MN$ and $\angle BAC=2\angle ABC$.
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $$f(1)+f(2)+\cdots+f(n)=n^2f(n)$$ for all positive integers $n$. If $f(1)=1003$, find the value of $f(2006)$.
Let $a_1=6,\ldots,a_n=6^{a_{n-1}}$. Find the remainder when $a_{100}$ is divided by $11$.
Let $-1<y<0<x<1$. If $A=x^2y$, $B=\frac{1}{x^2y}$, $C=y^2x$ and $D=\frac{1}{xy^2}$, arrange them from the smallest to the largest value.
One side of a triangle is $4$ cm. The other two sides are in the ratio $1:3$. Find the largest possible area of this triangle.
Simplify $\log_2 4\cdot\log_4 6\cdot\log_6 8\cdots\log_{2n}(2n+2)$.
Write $580$ as a sum of two squares.
Let $f$ be a function defined on the set of non-negative integers satisfying $$f(2n+1)=f(n),\qquad f(2n)=1-f(n).$$ Find $f(2007)$.
Let $f,g$ be two functions defined on $[0,2c]$, where $c>0$. Show that there exist $x,y\in[0,2c]$ such that $$|xy-f(x)+g(y)|\ge c^2.$$

Two circles of radii $1$ and $2$ are externally tangent to each other. A third circle is drawn tangent to both circles so that the centres of the three circles form a right triangle. Find the radius of the third circle.
Determine the maximum value of $m^2+n^2$, where $m,n\in\{1,2,3,\ldots,2007\}$ and $(n^2-mn-m^2)^2=1$.
Simplify $$\left[1+n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)\right]^{\frac12}.$$

Given a triangle $ABC$ and straight lines $DE$, $FG$, $HI$ such that $DE$ is parallel to $BC$, $FG$ is parallel to $AB$ and $HI$ is parallel to $CA$. The lines $DE$, $FG$, $HI$ meet at $O$. The areas of the triangles $DOH$, $EOG$ and $FOI$ are $4$, $9$ and $49$ respectively. Find the area of the triangle $ABC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2008_p3_fig.png
Determine how many four-digit numbers starting with $3$ have exactly two equal digits (for example $3447$, $3005$ or $3243$, but not $3388$).

$ABDC$ is a rectangle with $AB=12$ and $AD=24$ (see the figure). All the dashed lines in the diagram are parallel to $AB$. Find the length of the shortest dashed line.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2008_p5_fig.png

Let $ABCD$ be a square. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$ and $N$ the midpoint of $BC$. The lines $AN$ and $DM$ meet at $P$, the lines $AN$ and $CM$ meet at $Q$, and the lines $CM$ and $DN$ meet at $R$. Show that $$[AMP]+[BMQN]+[CNR]=[DPQR],$$ where $[\mathcal{F}]$ denotes the area of the figure $\mathcal{F}$.
Find positive integers $p$, $q$ and $n$ such that $p$ and $q$ are primes and $$\frac1p+\frac1q+\frac1{pq}=\frac1n.$$

In a mathematics competition the following problem was given: write four digits after the number $2009$ so that the new number obtained is divisible by $2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9$ and $10$. How many answers does this problem have?

A function $f$ is defined for any two positive integers $a$ and $b$ by
$$f(a,b)=\begin{cases} a & \text{if } a=b;\\ f(a-b,b) & \text{if } a>b;\\ f(b-a,a) & \text{if } a<b.\end{cases}$$
Compute the value of $f(17,9)$.
Find the area of the trapezium $ABCD$ with $AB$ parallel to $CD$, if it is known that $BC=3$, $AC=4$ and $AB=2CD=2AD$.
A square $S$ with integer side length can be divided into $25$ smaller squares with integer side lengths. All of these squares, except one, have side length $1$. Find the area of $S$.

Let $f(n)$ be the product $$f(n)=(\log_2 3)(\log_3 4)(\log_4 5)\cdots(\log_{n-1} n).$$
Find the value of $$f(4)+f(8)+f(16)+\cdots+f(2^{10}).$$
A quadrilateral $ABCD$ with sides $AB=25$, $BC=39$, $CD=52$ and $DA=60$ is placed in a circle so that $A,B,C,D$ lie on the circle. Find the diameter of the circle.

Given $n$ numbers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$, their \emph{supersum} $S$ is defined as $$S=\frac{s_1+s_2+\cdots+s_n}{n},\qquad\text{where } s_k=a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_k\ (k=1,2,\ldots,n).$$
If the supersum of $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{99}$ equals $1000$, find the supersum of $1,a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{99}$.

Two students play a game. The first player chooses three nonzero numbers. The second player then puts these numbers in place of the stars in the equation $$\star x^2+\star x+\star=0$$ in any order he likes. The first player wins if the resulting quadratic equation has two different rational roots. Otherwise the second player wins. Prove that the first player can always win. (A rational number is a number that can be written in the form $a/b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.)

Points $D$, $E$ and $F$ are chosen on the sides $AB$, $BC$, $AC$ of a triangle $ABC$ so that $DE=BE$ and $FE=CE$. Prove that the circumcentre of the triangle $ADF$ lies on the bisector of the angle $DEF$.

In the diagram, the congruent rectangles $ABCD$ and $DEFG$ have a common vertex $D$. The sides $BC$ and $EF$ meet at $H$. Given $DA=DE=8$, $AB=EF=12$ and $BH=7$, find the area of $ABHED$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2010_p1_fig.png

Let $N=\overline{abc}$ be a three-digit number. It is known that we can construct an isosceles triangle with $a$, $b$ and $c$ as the lengths of its sides. Determine how many such three-digit numbers $N$ there are.
($N=\overline{abc}$ means that $a$, $b$ and $c$ are the digits of $N$, and not $N=a\times b\times c$.)

A semicircle has diameter $XY$. A square $PQRS$ with side length $12$ is inscribed in the semicircle with $P$ and $S$ on the diameter. The square $STUV$ has $T$ on $RS$, $U$ on the semicircle and $V$ on $XY$. What is the area of $STUV$?
Let $n$ be an integer greater than $1$. If all the digits of $97n$ are odd, find the smallest possible value of $n$.

Find the smallest integer $k\ge 3$ with the property that it is possible to choose two of the numbers $1,2,\ldots,k$ in such a way that their product is equal to the sum of the remaining $k-2$ numbers.
A line segment of length $1$ is given in the plane. Show that a line segment of length $\sqrt{2010}$ can be constructed using only a straightedge and a compass.
Show that $$\log_a bc+\log_b ca+\log_c ab\ge 4\left(\log_{ab}c+\log_{bc}a+\log_{ca}b\right)$$ for all $a,b,c$ greater than $1$.
Show that there exist integers $m$ and $n$ such that $$\frac mn=\sqrt[3]{\sqrt{50}+7}-\sqrt[3]{\sqrt{50}-7}.$$

We inscribe a square in a circle. Then we inscribe a circle in this square, then a square in the inner circle, and so on. How many squares do we have to inscribe before the radius of the next circle is smaller than $\frac13$ of the radius of the original circle?
(A square is inscribed in a circle if all its vertices lie on the circle. A circle is inscribed in a square if it touches all the sides of the square.)

The numbers $\log_{10}(p^3q^7)$, $\log_{10}(p^5q^{12})$ and $\log_{10}(p^8q^{15})$ are the first three terms of an arithmetic progression. The $12$th term of this progression is $\log_{10}q^n$. Find the value of $n$.
How many triangles are there with integer sides and perimeter $30$? (Two congruent triangles are counted only once.)

A circle with centre at the origin is given. Let $s$ be an arc of the circle lying entirely in the first quadrant, and let $D$ and $E$ be the endpoints of $s$. The region lying below $s$, bounded by $s$, the $x$-axis and the vertical lines through $D$ and $E$, has area $1957$. The region lying to the left of $s$, bounded by $s$, the $y$-axis and the horizontal lines through $D$ and $E$, has area $2011$. Find the area of the sector $ODE$.
A function $P(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$ is given. It is known that $P(1)=2$, $P(2)=4$, $P(3)=8$ and $P(4)=16$. Find $P(5)$.

A positive integer $n$ is called \emph{good} if there exists an integer $k$ such that $$n=\left\lfloor\frac{2011}{k}\right\rfloor.$$
What is the smallest positive integer that is not good?
(Here $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the integer part of $x$, the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. For example, $\lfloor 3.1\rfloor=3$, $\lfloor 3.6\rfloor=3$, $\lfloor 3\rfloor=3$.)

A regular $2011$-gon $A_1A_2\ldots A_{2011}$ with centre $O$ is given. On each segment $OA_k$ ($k=1,2,\ldots,2011$) a point $B_k$ is chosen such that $$OB_k=\frac{OA_k}{k}.$$
Let $A$ and $B$ denote the areas of the polygons $A_1A_2\ldots A_{2011}$ and $B_1B_2\ldots B_{2011}$ respectively. Find the value of $A/B$.

For each positive integer $n$ let $$A_n=n^4-360n^2+400.$$
(a) Write $A_n$ as a product of two expressions of the form $an^2+bn+c$, where $a,b,c$ are integers.
(b) What is the sum of all the values of $A_n$ that are prime?

A $7\times 7$ chessboard is divided into $49$ unit squares. We are supplied with two types of tiles: \emph{Elbow} (\emph{Sesiku}) and \emph{Snake} (\emph{Ular}), as in the figure. The Elbow tile consists of $3$ squares and the Snake tile of $4$ squares. The tiles may be rotated and reflected. Our task is to cover the whole board with Elbow and Snake tiles without overlaps. Prove that we must use exactly one Snake.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2011_p9_fig.png
Find the area of a convex quadrilateral which has perpendicular diagonals of lengths $15$ and $18$.
A sequence $a_0,a_1,a_2,\ldots$ is defined by $a_0=2012$ and $a_{k+1}=a_k^2+1$ for all $k\ge 0$. Find the last digit of $a_{2012}$.
Three distinct positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ are given such that $a!\,b!\,c!=10!$. Find the number of possible values of $a+b+c$.
An obtuse triangle has side lengths $d$, $30$, $40$, where $d$ is an integer. How many possible values of $d$ are there?
The product of two four-digit positive integers is $4^8+6^8+9^8$. What is the smaller integer?
A positive integer ending with $8888$ has $16$ odd positive divisors. How many even positive divisors does this number have?

A triangle $ABC$ and a point $M$ on the side $BC$ are given. Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be the circumcircles of the triangles $ABM$ and $ACM$ respectively. The perpendicular bisector of $BC$ meets $AM$ at $P$. The line $BP$ meets $\Gamma_1$ at $D$ (different from $B$), and the line $CP$ meets $\Gamma_2$ at $E$ (different from $C$). Prove that $ED$ is parallel to $BC$.

Let $$T_n=1+\frac1n-\frac1{n^2}-\frac1{n^3}.$$
Find the smallest integer $k$ such that $$T_2T_3T_4\cdots T_k>2012.$$

There are $15$ keys on a keyboard, arranged in a straight line. Two keys are one \emph{semitone} apart if they are adjacent, and one \emph{tone} apart if they are separated by one key. A \emph{general scale} is a sequence of keys from left to right such that the first key of the sequence is the leftmost key, and any two consecutive keys of the sequence are either one tone or one semitone apart. Find the number of general scales with $8$ keys.
A large cube is divided into $99$ cubes with integer side lengths, $98$ of which have side $1$. Find the volume of the large cube.
Let $M$ be the set of all nine-digit positive integers that contain each of the digits from $1$ to $9$ exactly once. Find the greatest common divisor of all the elements of $M$.
What is the remainder when $5^{5555}$ is divided by $10\,000$?
A trapezium has perpendicular diagonals and height $12$. The length of one of its diagonals is $15$. Find the area of the trapezium.

The digits of $2013$ can be rearranged to form an arithmetic progression. Determine the number of four-digit positive integers with this property. (An arithmetic progression may have common difference $0$.)
Determine the smallest prime factor of $8051$.

A triangle $ABC$ is given. The midpoints of $AB$, $BC$, $CA$ are $C_1$, $A_1$, $B_1$ respectively. Construct another triangle $DEF$ with side lengths equal to $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$.
(a) Prove that the ratio of the area of the triangle $DEF$ to the area of the triangle $ABC$ is a constant, regardless of the choice of the triangle $ABC$.
(b) Find the area of the triangle $DEF$ if $AB=13$, $BC=14$, $CA=15$.
Prove that there exist integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_{2013},b$, all greater than $1$, such that $$(a_1!)(a_2!)(a_3!)\cdots(a_{2013}!)=b!.$$
A sequence $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots$ is defined as follows: $x_1=1$, $x_2=143$ and $$x_{n+1}=\frac{5(x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n)}{n}$$ for all $n\ge 2$. Prove that all the terms of the sequence are integers.

The following figure is made up of sides with lengths $x$ and $y$. Adjacent sides are perpendicular. If both the perimeter and the area of the figure are equal to $24$, what is $x^2$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2014_p1_fig.png
Fill in the missing digit in the following statement: the greatest common divisor of $\square 829783$ and $9999$ is $3$.
Ana was born exactly $12!$ seconds ago. Her latest birthday was her $N$th. What is $N$?

In the diagram, the points $A$, $B$, $C$ lie on a line, and there are two circles with diameters $AB$ and $BC$ respectively. A line is tangent to the two circles at the points $D$ and $E$. Let $F$ be the midpoint of $DE$. If $AB=18$ and $BC=8$, find the area of the triangle $AFC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2014_p4_fig.png

There are $n$ girls in a school, and they decide to hold a popularity contest. Each girl ranks the other $n-1$ girls from $1$ to $n-1$ (rank $1$ for the most favourite person and rank $n-1$ for the least favourite one). Then each girl adds up all the ranks given to her by the other girls. When the results were announced, the first place winner scored $100$, and the second place winner scored $139$. What is the maximum possible value of $n$?

A trapezium $ABCD$ with $AB$ parallel to $DC$ and $DC>AB$ is given. Points $M$ and $N$ are chosen on the sides $AD$ and $BC$ respectively such that $MN$ is parallel to $AB$ and the area of $ABNM$ is equal to the area of $MNCD$. Prove that the area of the triangle $BNM$ is greater than the area of the triangle $NCD$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2014_p7_fig.png

A subset of $\{1,2,3,\ldots,2014\}$ is called \emph{good} if (a) it does not contain both elements $1$ and $2$; (b) the sum of its elements is divisible by $3$. For example, the subset $\{1,23,456,789\}$ is good. Find the number of good subsets. (The sum of the elements of the empty set is $0$.)
Prove that there are infinitely many pairs of real numbers $(x,y)$ such that $x\ne y$ and $x^y=y^x$.

Five points $O$, $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$ and $P_4$ are given such that $\angle OP_1P_2=\angle OP_2P_3=\angle OP_3P_4=90^\circ$. It is also given that $P_1P_2=9$, $P_2P_3=29$ and $P_3P_4=33$. If the length of $OP_4$ is $\sqrt{2015}$, what is the length of $OP_1$?
It is given that the value of $\log_2 3$ is approximately $1.585$. Find the nearest integer to the value of $k$ that satisfies the equation $$2^k=1.5^{12}.$$
For any integer $n>1$, we define $A_n$ as the product of $n$ with the smallest prime factor of $n$. How many $n$ are there that satisfy $A_n\le 100$?

A triangle $ABC$ with $AB=AC=40$ and $BC=48$ is given. A circle $T_1$ is tangent to all the sides of the triangle. Another circle $T_2$ is tangent to the side $AB$, the side $AC$ and the circle $T_1$. What is the radius of $T_2$?
Two positive numbers $x$ and $y$ with $x>y$ are given such that $$x^2+y^2=\frac{1201}{600}xy.$$ Find the value of $\dfrac{x+y}{x-y}$.
The product $$\frac12\cdot\frac24\cdot\frac38\cdot\frac4{16}\cdots\frac{99}{2^{99}}\cdot\frac{100}{2^{100}}$$ is written as a fraction in lowest terms. What is the last digit of the denominator?

A triangle $ABC$ is given. Let $B'$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and let $C'$ be the midpoint of $AB$. The lines $BB'$ and $CC'$ meet at $M$. It is known that there is a circle that is tangent to all the sides of the quadrilateral $AB'MC'$. Prove that $AB=AC$.

A subset of $\{1,2,3,\ldots,2015\}$ is called \emph{good} if the following condition is fulfilled: for any element $x$ of the subset, the sum of all the other elements of the subset has the same last digit as $x$. For example, $\{10,20,30\}$ is a good subset since $10$ has the same last digit as $20+30=50$, $20$ has the same last digit as $10+30=40$, and $30$ has the same last digit as $10+20=30$.
(a) Find an example of a good subset with $400$ elements.
(b) Prove that there is no good subset with $405$ elements.

There are $200$ numbers on a blackboard: $$1!,\ 2!,\ 3!,\ 4!,\ \ldots,\ 199!,\ 200!.$$
Julia erases one of the numbers. When Julia multiplies the remaining $199$ numbers, the product is a perfect square. Which number was erased?
Find the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ with interior angles $\angle A=\angle B=\angle C=45^\circ$, $\angle D=225^\circ$, and $BD=12$.
Determine the number of integers $n$ that satisfy the inequality $$\left|\sqrt2-\sqrt n\right|<1.$$

There are $20$ members in a badminton club. The club coach wants to select two members of the same gender to represent the club in a doubles game. There are $99$ possible choices. If the club has more female than male members, how many female members are there?
A right triangle has two sides of lengths $39$ and $89$. The third side also has integer length. A circle lies inside the triangle, tangent to all three sides. What is the radius of the circle?

An integer is called \emph{squareful} if it is divisible by a perfect square other than $1$. For example, $99$ is squareful because it is divisible by $9=3^2$. Find a positive integer $N<50$ such that all three numbers $N$, $N+1$ and $N+2$ are squareful.
The number $50^k$ has exactly $2016$ positive divisors. What is the value of $k$?

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ which is not a rectangle is given. Let $O$ be the midpoint of $AB$. A circle with centre $O$ is tangent to the sides $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$. Prove that $$\frac{AB}{2}=\sqrt{AD\times BC}.$$

Hawa writes down the base-$10$ expansion of the number $2^{2016}$ in her notebook. Adam writes down the base-$10$ expansion of the number $5^{2016}$ in his notebook. What is the total number of digits that they have written down?
Let $n>1$ be an integer. Prove that $n^{n-1}-1$ is divisible by $(n-1)^2$.

A circle $\Gamma$ and a point $P$ outside $\Gamma$ are given. Points $A$ and $B$ lie on $\Gamma$ such that the lines $PA$ and $PB$ are tangent to $\Gamma$, and $\angle APB=36^\circ$. Let $C$ be a point on the major arc $AB$. What is $\angle ACB$, in degrees?
It is given that $k!=1!\times 3!\times 5!\times 7!$. Determine the value of $k$.
It is given that $a_n=n^n$ for all positive integers $n$. Among the values $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_{1000}$, how many are perfect cubes?
The height of the triangle $ABC$ from the vertex $A$ is $h_A$, and from the vertex $B$ it is $h_B$. It is given that $h_A\ge BC$ and $h_B\ge AC$. Find $\angle BAC$, in degrees.

A prime number $p$ is called a \emph{Friedlander--Iwaniec prime} if it can be expressed as $p=a^4+b^2$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. For example, $2017$ is a Friedlander--Iwaniec prime since $2017=3^4+44^2$. How many Friedlander--Iwaniec primes less than $100$ are there?
Numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are given such that $$\frac{(a-b)(c-d)}{(b-c)(d-a)}=-\frac16.$$ Find the value of $\dfrac{(a-c)(b-d)}{(a-b)(c-d)}$.

A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given. The points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of the sides $BC$ and $CD$ respectively. The sides of the triangle $AMN$ cut the quadrilateral into four triangles. Suppose that the areas of these triangles are four consecutive integers. What is the largest possible area of the triangle $ABD$? (A quadrilateral is convex if each of its interior angles is less than $180^\circ$.)

(a) A positive number $n$ is given. A triangle has side lengths $2n+1$, $2n^2+2n$ and $2n^2+2n+1$. Prove that the triangle is a right triangle.
(b) Prove that there exist $2017$ positive integers $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_{2017}$ such that each of the following numbers is a perfect square: $$a_1^2,\quad a_1^2+a_2^2,\quad a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2,\quad\ldots,\quad a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2+a_4^2+\cdots+a_{2017}^2.$$

A positive integer $n$ is given. Consider all the subsets of $\{1,2,3,\ldots,n\}$ except the empty set. For each subset consider the fraction $\frac1d$, where $d$ is the product of all the elements of the subset. Let $S_n$ be the sum of these fractions taken over all the subsets. For example, for $n=3$ the nonempty subsets of $\{1,2,3\}$ are $\{1\}$, $\{2\}$, $\{3\}$, $\{1,2\}$, $\{1,3\}$, $\{2,3\}$ and $\{1,2,3\}$, therefore $$S_3=\frac11+\frac12+\frac13+\frac1{1\cdot2}+\frac1{1\cdot3}+\frac1{2\cdot3}+\frac1{1\cdot2\cdot3}=1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac12+\frac13+\frac16+\frac16=3.$$
Prove that $S_n=n$ for all positive integers $n$.
A cuboid has integer volume. Three of its faces have different areas, namely $7$, $27$ and $L$. What is the smallest possible integer value of $L$?
Let $a$ and $b$ be prime numbers such that $a+b=10000$. Find the sum of the smallest possible value of $a$ and the largest possible value of $a$.
A regular polygon with $n$ sides is given. It is known that there are $1200$ ways to choose three of its vertices so that they form the vertices of a right triangle. What is the value of $n$?

A circle with diameter $AB$ is given. Points $C$ and $D$ are selected on the circumference so that the chord $CD$ intersects $AB$ inside the circle, at the point $P$. The ratio of the arc length $\widehat{AC}$ to the arc length $\widehat{BD}$ is $4:1$, while the ratio of the arc length $\widehat{AD}$ to the arc length $\widehat{BC}$ is $3:2$. Find $\angle APC$, in degrees.
Determine the value of $$(101\times 99)-(102\times 98)+(103\times 97)-(104\times 96)+\cdots+(149\times 51)-(150\times 50).$$
Determine the smallest prime $p$ such that $2018!$ is divisible by $p^3$ but not divisible by $p^4$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $D$ be the reflection of the point $B$ in the line $AC$, and let $E$ be the reflection of the point $C$ in the line $AB$. Let $\Gamma_1$ be the circle through $A$, $B$ and $D$, and $\Gamma_2$ the circle through $A$, $C$ and $E$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ other than $A$. Let $\Gamma$ be the circle through $A$, $B$ and $C$. Show that the centre of $\Gamma$ lies on the line $AP$.

Let $\{a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots\}$ be the set of all integers that can be expressed as a sum of four distinct positive fourth powers, with $a_1<a_2<a_3<\cdots$. If $a_i=2018$, find the value of $i$. (A positive fourth power is a number of the form $k^4$, where $k$ is a positive integer.)

For any positive integer $k$, denote by $g_k$ the largest odd divisor of $k$. For example, $g_8=1$, $g_9=9$ and $g_{10}=5$.
(a) Prove that $g_{n+1}+g_{n+2}+\cdots+g_{2n}=n^2$ for all positive integers $n$.
(b) Find the value of $g_1+g_2+g_3+\cdots+g_{512}$.

Determine the value of $$\frac{1}{\log_2\frac17}+\frac{1}{\log_3\frac17}+\frac{1}{\log_4\frac17}+\frac{1}{\log_5\frac17}+\frac{1}{\log_6\frac17}-\frac{1}{\log_7\frac17}-\frac{1}{\log_8\frac17}-\frac{1}{\log_9\frac17}-\frac{1}{\log_{10}\frac17}.$$

A regular pentagram $ABCDE$ with area $100$ is given, as shown below. The lines $AB$ and $DE$ meet at $M$. The lines $AE$ and $BC$ meet at $N$. Find the area of the quadrilateral $CDMN$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/myo_2019_p2_fig.png

An integer is called a \emph{factorion} if it is equal to the sum of the factorials of all its digits. For example, $40585$ is a factorion since $$4!+0!+5!+8!+5!=24+1+120+40320+120=40585.$$
Find a three-digit factorion.

Consider the set $A=\{1,2,3,4,5,\ldots,100\}$. For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $A$ in which no two elements differ by $k$. Determine the number of possible values of $k$ for which $f(k)=50$.
A triangle $ABC$ and a point $D$ on the side $AB$ are given. It is known that $BC=28$, $AD=25$, $BD=24$ and $CD=20$. Find the length of $AC$.
It is known that $$2018\left(2019^{39}+2019^{37}+2019^{35}+\cdots+2019^5+2019^3+2019\right)+1$$ is a prime number. Determine the number of positive divisors of $2019^{41}+1$.

Maslina chooses three real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$. Then she writes the following equation in the variable $x$: $$\left(\frac1{x+a}-\frac1x\right)+\left(\frac1{x+b}-\frac1x\right)+\left(\frac1{x+c}-\frac1x\right)=0.$$
Prove that, whatever the choice of $a$, $b$ and $c$, the equation has at least one real solution.
A parallelogram $ABCD$ is given. A point $M$ is chosen such that $\angle MAC=\angle DAC$ and $\angle MBD=\angle CBD$. Prove that $$\frac{AM}{BM}=\left(\frac{AC}{BD}\right)^2.$$

We call a sequence of five numbers \emph{good} if it is an arithmetic progression that contains the terms $20$ and $19$. For example, the following two sequences are good: $$18,\ 19,\ 20,\ 21,\ 22;\qquad 20,\ 19\tfrac23,\ 19\tfrac13,\ 19,\ 18\tfrac23.$$
For each good sequence we take the sum of all its terms. Then we add these sums over all possible good sequences. What is the result?
If $\log_4(x+2y)+\log_4(x-2y)=1$, find the minimum value of $\sqrt3\,(|x|-|y|)$.

Let $A=(0,2)$, and let $B$ and $C$ be two points on the parabola $y^2=x+4$ such that $AB\perp BC$. The range of the $y$-coordinate of the point $C$ can be written in the form $y\le p$ or $y\ge q$. Determine the value of $q$.
Let $b_n=6^n+8^n$. For example, $b_1=6+8=14$ and $b_2=6^2+8^2=100$, so $b_{2021}=6^{2021}+8^{2021}$. Determine the remainder when $b_{2021}$ is divided by $49$.
Bala has $10$ Mathematics books, while Hassilah has $12$ Science books. In how many ways can $4$ books belonging to Bala be exchanged for $5$ books belonging to Hassilah?
If the polynomial $x^4+ax^3+2x^2+bx+1$ has a real root, then $a^2+b^2\ge p$. Find the value of $p$.

Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^2}{x^2+1}$. Find the value of $$f\left(\frac1{2021}\right)+f\left(\frac2{2021}\right)+\cdots+f\left(\frac{2020}{2021}\right)+f\left(\frac{2021}{2021}\right)+f\left(\frac{2021}{2020}\right)+\cdots+f\left(\frac{2021}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{2021}{1}\right).$$

(a) If $p$ is a prime number, show that $(p+1)^p-1$ is divisible by $p^2$ for all positive integers $n$.
(b) Find the last digit of the number $$1^1+2^2+3^3+\cdots+2021^2.$$
Prove that for all real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ the following inequality holds: $$x^2+y^2+z^2-xy-yz-zx\ge\frac34(x-y)^2.$$
Two positive integers $a$ and $b$ are such that the numbers $15a+16b$ and $16a-15b$ are both squares of positive integers. Find the least possible value of the smaller of these two squares.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that $a<b$. The greatest common divisor and the lowest common multiple of $a$ and $b$ are $7$ and $630$, respectively. Find the sum of all possible values of $b-a$.
The integer $\overline{2022XYZ2022}$ is divisible by $99$, where $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are digits, not necessarily distinct. Find the sum of all possible values of $X+Y+Z$.

$ABC$ is a triangle with a right angle at $B$ and $AB=BC=12$. The altitude from $B$ meets the line $AC$ at the point $D$. Another line is drawn from the point $A$ to the midpoint of $BC$. Let $E$ be the point of intersection of these two lines. Find the area of the triangle $ADE$.

The number $2022$ is called \emph{heavy}, because the larger digit value appears strictly more often than the smaller digit value. Using only the digits from $1$ to $9$, how many heavy $5$-digit numbers are there? (Note: $333$ is not considered heavy, as it has only one distinct digit value.)

The date $22/02/2022$ (in the form DD/MM/YYYY) is called \emph{wonderful}, since $22022022$ is a palindromic number, that is, a number that reads the same forwards and backwards. Counting the date itself, how many days does it take to reach the next wonderful date?
Let $x$ be a real number such that $x^3+\dfrac1{x^3}=18$. Evaluate $x^2+\dfrac1{x^2}$.

A circle with centre $O$ and diameter $AOB$ is given. The diameter is extended beyond $B$ to the point $C$ so that $AB=BC$. A line through $C$ is tangent to the circle at the point $D$. Prove that $\dfrac{AD}{BD}=\sqrt2$.

Evaluate the expression $$\left(\sqrt{1\cdot2}+\frac{9}{\sqrt{1\cdot2}}\right)^2+\left(\sqrt{2\cdot3}+\frac{9}{\sqrt{2\cdot3}}\right)^2+\cdots+\left(\sqrt{80\cdot81}+\frac{9}{\sqrt{80\cdot81}}\right)^2.$$
Determine the largest integer $n$ such that $10^n$ divides $2022!$.

The real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy the system of equations below. What is the value of $k$?
$$\begin{aligned}a+b+c&=7,\\ a^2+b^2+c^2&=17,\\ abc&=12,\\ a^2(b+c)+b^2(c+a)+c^2(a+b)&=k.\end{aligned}$$
Yong Chin wants to form $4$-digit even numbers with distinct digits, using the digits from $1$ to $6$. What is the sum of all such numbers?

The squares $A_0B_0C_0D_0$, $A_1B_1C_1D_1$, $A_2B_2C_2D_2$, $\ldots$, $A_nB_nC_nD_n$ are stacked on top of each other, forming a cuboid. The vertical distance between consecutive squares is $1$. Find the smallest value of $n>1$ such that $\dfrac{A_nC_0}{A_1C_0}$ is an integer.
Find the remainder when $2023^{2023^{2023}}$ is divided by $25$.

Som has a triangular sheet of paper $ABC$. She folds the paper so that the point $A$ falls on the line $BC$ and the fold line is parallel to $BC$. She unfolds it and folds the paper again so that the two parallel lines (the fold line and $BC$) meet, and repeats the folding a third time. Then Som unfolds the paper and highlights all the fold lines created. If the length of $BC$ is $16$, find the total length of all the highlighted lines.

How many integer solutions are there to the following equation?
$$a^7b^{17}=2023^{2023}$$
Simplify the following sum to a single fraction: $$\sum_{k=1}^{2023}\frac{k^2-k-1}{(k+1)!}.$$
$ABCDEFGH$ is a regular octagon with side length $1$. The lines $AD$ and $BH$ intersect at the point $X$. Find the length of $AX$.
What is the largest positive integer $n$ such that $n^3+1023$ is divisible by both $n+7$ and $n-3$?

Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be real numbers satisfying the following system of equations:
$$\begin{aligned}(a-b)(c-b)&=6,\\ (b-a)(c-a)&=3,\\ (a-c)(b-c)&=-2.\end{aligned}$$
If $a+b+c=7$, evaluate $a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc$.

$ABCDEF$ is a regular hexagon with side length $1$. A point $P$ outside the hexagon is such that $PBD$ is an equilateral triangle. It is known that the area of $PBCD$ is $\sqrt{\dfrac ab}$, where $a$ and $b$ are coprime. Evaluate $a+b$.
How many four-digit positive integers contain at least one digit $4$ or are divisible by $4$?
Find the largest positive integer that has no repeated digits and is divisible by $99$.

The floor function $\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. For example, $\lfloor 2.3\rfloor=\lfloor 2.7\rfloor=2$ and $\lfloor 5\rfloor=5$. Evaluate $$\lfloor\sqrt1\rfloor+\lfloor\sqrt2\rfloor+\lfloor\sqrt3\rfloor+\cdots+\lfloor\sqrt{225}\rfloor.$$

A number is called \emph{sum perfect} if its last digit is equal to the sum of all its preceding digits. For example, $2024$ is sum perfect, because $2+0+2=4$. How many four-digit sum perfect numbers are there?

For every positive integer $n\ge 2$, write $n$ as a product of at least two positive integers, that is, $n=a_1\times a_2\times\cdots\times a_k$ for some $k\ge 2$. Find all $n$ for which the equation $$n=a_1\times a_2\times\cdots\times a_k=a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_k$$ can be satisfied.
Simplify the following sum: $$\sum_{n=0}^{10}\frac{2^n(n-1)}{(n+1)!}.$$

A triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle with centre $O$, where $\angle OAC=\angle OBC$ and $\angle ACB$ is acute. Prove that the ratio of the area of the triangle $ABC$ to the area of the triangle $ABO$ is equal to $\sec(\angle ACB)+1$.
